title: Regularity is unchanged on completing the base of a continuous adic map
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian quasi-excellent ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-exc-excellent-ring], let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal and put $C=\widehat A_I=\varprojlim_n A/I^n$, with canonical map $\iota:A\to C$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, let $J\subseteq B$ be an ideal such that $B\to\varprojlim_n B/J^n$ is an isomorphism, and let $u:C\to B$ be a ring homomorphism with $u(IC)B\subseteq J$. Then $u$ is a regular ring map if and only if $u\circ\iota:A\to B$ is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Here regular means flat, with Noetherian geometrically regular residue-field fibres. The ideals $IC$ and $J$ need not generate the same topology on $B$; neither $B$ nor $A\to B$ is required to be of finite type, and $B$ is not required to be quasi-excellent.

source.place: Temkin, arXiv:0904.1592v2, Lemma 2.4.4, printed p.16. The adic algebra formulation is written with an explicit ideal J of definition and I-image contained in J, as needed in Corollary 2.4.5. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: First suppose $u$ is regular. Quasi-excellence makes $A$ a G-ring, so $\iota:A\to C$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular]. For a prime $\mathfrak r\subset A$, the fibre $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ is a quotient of the localization of $B$ at the image of $A\setminus\mathfrak r$. This localization is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]; its quotients are Noetherian because an ideal in a quotient lifts to a finitely generated ideal upstairs. Thus the additional fibre-Noetherianity hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition] holds, and that lemma proves $u\iota$ regular.

For the converse assume $v=u\iota$ regular. The in-particular clause of [lem-per-quasi-excellent-formal-affines] makes $C$ Noetherian and quasi-excellent. It is therefore a G-ring by [def-exc-excellent-ring]; in particular, for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset C$, the canonical map $C_{\mathfrak p}\to\widehat{C_{\mathfrak p}}$ is regular by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. To apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal] to $u$, it suffices to prove regularity of $C_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ for every maximal $\mathfrak q\subset B$, where $\mathfrak p=u^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. If $B=0$, there are no such ideals and that criterion already gives the conclusion.

source.place: Tag 07C0 (lemma-regular-local); Temkin Lemma 2.4.4, converse, and Theorem 2.1.8 (Gabber).

proof.text: Every maximal $\mathfrak q\subset B$ contains $J$. Indeed for $x\in J$ and $b\in B$, the finite sums $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(bx)^i$ modulo $J^n$ are compatible and define, by the assumed isomorphism $B\cong\varprojlim B/J^n$, an inverse to $1-bx$. If $x\notin\mathfrak q$, its nonzero residue in the field $B/\mathfrak q$ has an inverse represented by some $b$, forcing the unit $1-bx$ into $\mathfrak q$, a contradiction. Hence $IC\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Set $\mathfrak r=\iota^{-1}(\mathfrak p)=v^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Since $A$ is Noetherian, $I$ is finitely generated. The canonical isomorphism $A/I\cong C/IC$ from [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] identifies the ideals $\mathfrak r/I$ and $\mathfrak p/IC$, so $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak rC$ and $A/\mathfrak r\cong C/\mathfrak p$. Localizing this quotient isomorphism at the nonzero elements gives $\kappa(\mathfrak r)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, induced by $\iota$; explicitly both are the fraction field of the same quotient domain.

source.place: Tags 05GI (algebra-lemma-radical-completion) and 05GG (algebra-lemma-hathat-finitely-generated); explicit quotient calculation for Temkin Lemma 2.4.4.

proof.text: Write $R=A_{\mathfrak r}$, $D=C_{\mathfrak p}$, $T=B_{\mathfrak q}$, $a:R\to D$ and $f:D\to T$ for the induced local maps, so $g=fa:R\to T$ is the local map of $v$. The completion map $\iota$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat], and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] makes $a$ flat. The rings $R,D,T$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Step 3 gives $\mathfrak rD=\mathfrak pD$ and an isomorphism on residue fields. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-completion-iso] supplies the canonical isomorphism $\widehat a:\widehat R\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat D$, compatible with the canonical completion maps. Also [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal], applied to the assumed regular map $v$, makes $g$ regular, in particular flat with geometrically regular closed fibre.

Complete the local maps at their maximal ideals. On each quotient level composition sends the class of $r\in R$ to the class of $g(r)=f(a(r))$, so the induced maps satisfy $\widehat f\widehat a=\widehat g$. Since $g$ is flat, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-completion] makes $\widehat g$ flat. Since $\widehat a$ is an isomorphism, $\widehat f=\widehat g\widehat a^{-1}$ is flat (transport the defining tensor-injectivity condition along this ring isomorphism). The canonical map $D\to\widehat D$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat], so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp] makes $D\to\widehat T$ flat. The equality $\widehat f\iota_D=\iota_Tf$ follows on each quotient from the same formula. Finally $T\to\widehat T$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-algebra-faithfully-flat-descent] to $D\to T\to\widehat T$: $f$ is flat.

source.place: Tags 0C4G (lemma-flat-completion), 00MC (algebra-lemma-completion-faithfully-flat); Temkin Lemma 2.4.4, final flatness argument.

proof.text: The closed fibre of $f$ is $T/\mathfrak pT=T/\mathfrak rT$, by Step 3. Its structure field $D/\mathfrak pD=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is identified with $R/\mathfrak rR=\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ by that step, and the action on the quotient agrees: both send the class of $a\in A$ to the class of $v(a)$. Thus it is the geometrically regular closed fibre of $g$ from Step 4, with the same field action. By Step 2 the canonical map $D\to\widehat D$ is regular, and by Step 5 $f$ is flat. The new general criterion [lem-per-g-ring-local-closed-fibre-criterion] applies to the Noetherian local rings $D,T$ and proves $f$ regular. This holds for every maximal $\mathfrak q\subset B$, so [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal] proves $u$ regular.
